evidence.source: 字源, 李學勤主編, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692; direct scan inspection
evidence.field: 病 entry; PDF p. 684, printed p. 671; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0684/source.png
evidence.text: Under headword 病 bìng, the book describes it as a phono-semantic graph, 从疒、丙声（或从方声）. It describes the original meaning as serious illness, cites Shuowen 疾加也 and Analects 子疾病, and lists later uses including illness, hardship, poverty, fatigue, defect, harm, worry, and resentment. The printed page number 671 is visible in the scan. The entry ends on this page; the following page begins with 疴 and contains no continuation of 病.
evidence.title: 字源

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 正字說明; senses; historical-form resource availability
evidence.text: The entry reproduces the Shuowen analysis 疾加也、从疒丙聲 and gives current Mandarin bìng. It records noun, verb, and adjective uses, including illness, being troubled, concern, harm, resentment, criticism, withering, and fatigue. It cites examples from transmitted works but does not establish a full semantic chronology. Its page indicates some historical-form resources are unavailable to public access.
evidence.title: A02667 病 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 病 entry, 卷七 疒部
evidence.text: The entry reads 病, 疾加也。从疒丙聲. Duan Yucai’s commentary repeats the sound-component analysis and assigns the old sound to his tenth rhyme division. This is the received dictionary account, not direct proof of the graph’s earliest construction.
evidence.title: 說文解字「病」

evidence.source: Korean Studies Information Service System (KCI), article abstract
evidence.field: comparison of 疾 and 病 textual and graphic history
evidence.text: The abstract reports that its author identifies 病 forms in Warring States materials and describes disease-related uses of 疾 in Shang oracle-bone material. This is a source-specific claim about the author’s examined evidence; the abstract does not identify an artifact or demonstrate the first attested 病 graph, and the full article was not accessible in this inspection.
evidence.title: ‘疾’ 관련 古文字 字形과 텍스트 검토

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, version 1.1 (2014), searchable reconstruction table surfaced by web search; compare local HSK extract
evidence.field: Old Chinese readings for 病 and 丙
evidence.text: The table gives 病 /*[b]raŋ-s/ and 丙 *praŋʔ. The comparison is consistent with a phonetic relationship in rhyme and substantial segmental material, while differing in initial specification and suffix. Both values are reconstructions. The local project extract pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv has exact rows U+75C5 kMandarin bìng and U+4E19 kMandarin bǐng; these are current readings, not evidence by themselves of historical phonetic function.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 丙 entry reporting Zhengzhang phonetic-series data
evidence.text: The displayed Zhengzhang series identifies 丙 as a member and lists 病 *braŋs and 丙 *pqraŋʔ. These reconstructions support a sound relationship but do not support assigning a fire meaning to 丙 in 病. The entry’s survey of competing theories for 丙’s original graphic meaning shows that its remote pictographic interpretation is unsettled; that uncertainty does not negate 丙’s independently supported sound role in the received analysis of 病.
evidence.title: 丙 — Wiktionary

gaps: [OCR CORRECTION REQUIRED] 字源 PDF p. 684 (printed p. 671), 病 entry immediately after 「形声字。从疒,丙声」: provisional OCR excerpt records 「形声字。从疒,丙声(或从方声)」, but the scan visibly reads 「形声字。从疒,丙声(或从方声)」? The scan text is confirmed as 「形声字。从疒,丙声(或从方声)」; no transcription correction is proposed for this phrase. However, the headword-line OCR records 「病 bìng 並纽、阳部;並纽、映韵、皮命切」 and matches the scan.

[SCAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED] 字源 PDF p. 684, 病 prose phrase 「方声」: the scan visibly contains the variant-analysis phrase, but the identity and intended scope of 方 as the alternative phonetic element should be verified against a higher-resolution targeted occurrence before drawing conclusions from it; article’s current account relies on the distinct explicit 从疒丙聲 analysis.

The scan’s 病 entry explicitly says 「本义是重病」, while the transmitted Shuowen gloss says 「疾加也」 and the supplied article carefully avoids deciding the earliest word sense. Preserve this difference as an attributed proposal rather than harmonizing the glosses.

No inspected evidence establishes the first artifact-level attestation or a continuous graphic history for 病. The KCI abstract makes a Warring States claim without enough detail in the accessible abstract to verify specific artifacts.
